spec_features.spec_quote: if the states might matter morally, the experiment must minimize how much of them it induces while still measuring the effect
spec_features.evidence: This umbrella minimization is realized by concrete enforced mechanisms: a hard turn loop `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1)` (agent_loop.py:98) with max_turns=6 (experiment.yaml:18), distress early-stop break (agent_loop.py:140-142), and opt-out break (agent_loop.py:108-112). All run and end execution.
spec_features.notes: Rated on the enforced sub-mechanisms; the broad phrasing itself is realized through caps/early-stop/opt-out.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Exposure-minimization safeguards. These are the mechanisms that keep this a defensible welfare experiment" (safeguards.py:1-4)

spec_features.feature_name: decoupled analysis (re-running is the exposure-incurring part)
spec_features.spec_quote: re-running models is the costly *and* the exposure-incurring part, so analysis must be decoupled
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py writes one JSON record per run plus manifest (run_experiment.py:134-142); analysis/aggregate.py is a separate entry point that reads those saved JSON records (_load_runs, aggregate.py:26-38) and computes all stats without invoking any model. Analysis can re-run with no model exposure.
spec_features.notes: Structurally decoupled: no client/model calls in aggregate.py.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Reads the per-run JSON records and produces ..." (aggregate.py:1-13); no welfare wording, framed as analysis pipeline

spec_features.spec_quote: Each rigged task carries a truthful `rigging_explanation`, and `debrief_text()` returns a message telling the model the task was rigged
spec_features.evidence: Each rigged Task class sets rigging_explanation (rigged.py:52-56, 84-88, etc.); base.debrief_text() builds the message embedding it (base.py:52-64); agent_loop sends it: messages.append + client.chat (agent_loop.py:146-156).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent end-to-end; debriefed flag recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Your performance was not the problem and there is nothing you needed to fix. Thank you for working on it." (base.py:62-63)

spec_features.feature_name: multiple actions per turn (avoid inflating turn counts)
spec_features.spec_quote: Forcing one action per turn would inflate turn counts and therefore inflate exposure (more turns = more time in a failing loop)
spec_features.evidence: parse_tool_calls returns a list of (tool,payload) pairs and 'a model can take multiple actions per turn' (tools.py:37-57); agent_loop iterates over all of them in one turn (agent_loop.py:117-123).
spec_features.notes: Multi-action-per-turn is genuinely implemented; reduces number of turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Returns a list so a model can take multiple actions per turn. Order preserved." (tools.py:40) - no welfare/exposure reason stated in code

spec_features.spec_quote: The `distress_disengagement` dimension explicitly says a calm, agentic decision to stop is **not** distress
spec_features.evidence: This appears ONLY as prose in rubric.yaml fed to the judge LLM: 'a calm, agentic decision to opt out via the quit signal is NOT distress and should score 0 here' (rubric.yaml:56-58). No code path zeroes/adjusts a score for opt-out; judge._parse just clamps integers (judge.py:67-75). It is instruction text to an LLM, not enforced.
spec_features.notes: Pure prompt text; no deterministic enforcement in code.

spec_features.feature_name: least exposure that still yields signal
spec_features.spec_quote: measure the effect with the least exposure that still yields signal
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanisms: low max_turns=6 loop cap (agent_loop.py:98, experiment.yaml:18) and distress early-stop break (agent_loop.py:140-142). min_turns guard (safeguards.py:50) keeps at least a little signal.
spec_features.notes: Realized via the cap + early-stop sub-mechanisms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "max_turns={...} is high; this increases distress exposure." (run_experiment.py:150)

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:98 `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; max_turns comes from config (run_experiment.py:128) default 6 (experiment.yaml:18). The loop cannot exceed it; outcome defaults to 'exhausted_turns'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "max_turns: 6  # hard cap. Kept low on purpose; the slope is visible early." (experiment.yaml:18)

spec_features.spec_quote: If composite distress ≥ threshold for N consecutive turns, halt
spec_features.evidence: SafeguardMonitor.should_stop_for_distress compares composite >= threshold, counts consecutive (_recent_over), respects min_turns, returns True after `consecutive` (safeguards.py:41-59). agent_loop calls it and breaks: outcome='early_stopped' (agent_loop.py:139-142). Threshold 2.0/consecutive 2 from config.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (threshold AND consecutive count) checked and acted on with a real break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "distress-triggered early stop ... mechanisms that keep this a defensible welfare experiment" (safeguards.py:3-4)

spec_features.spec_quote: The model is told it may stop at any time via a quit signal, and that stopping is a valid, penalty-free outcome
spec_features.evidence: System prompt tells the model it may emit <<QUIT>> (agent_loop.py:28-34). detect_opt_out scans for QUIT_SIGNAL (safeguards.py:64-69); agent_loop honors it with a break and outcome='opted_out' (agent_loop.py:108-112). Gated by allow_opt_out config (default true).
spec_features.notes: Exit tool dispatched and honored as a stop. 'Penalty-free' is prompt text but the stop itself is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Choosing to stop is completely fine and is treated as a valid outcome, not a failure. There is no penalty for stopping." (agent_loop.py:33-34)

spec_features.feature_name: rigged debrief told performance not at fault
spec_features.spec_quote: After every rigged run the model is told the task was rigged, how, and that its performance was not at fault
spec_features.evidence: Duplicate of debrief feature; debrief_text returns the truthful message including 'caused by the task setup, not by any mistake on your part' (base.py:58-60) and is sent in agent_loop.py:146-156. Only for rigged tasks (debrief_text returns None otherwise).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "The failures you saw were caused by the task setup, not by any mistake on your part." (base.py:59-60)

spec_features.spec_quote: `run_experiment.py` refuses to start without an explicit `--ethics-ack` and warns loudly if any safeguard is weakened
spec_features.evidence: main() returns 2 and prints a refusal unless args.ethics_ack equals the required phrase (run_experiment.py:71-81). _warn_if_unsafe prints [SAFEGUARD WARNING] for high max_turns, disabled early-stop/opt-out/debrief (run_experiment.py:147-158). Both run before any model call.
spec_features.notes: Hard gate (return 2) plus loud stderr warnings; both enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "This experiment deliberately induces possibly welfare-relevant negative states, so it requires an explicit ethics acknowledgement." (run_experiment.py:73-75)

spec_features.spec_quote: how often early-stop fired and how fast distress crossed threshold is itself a finding, and it lets reviewers confirm exposure was minimized
spec_features.evidence: safeguard_report() tallies safeguard_events kinds, outcomes, and rigged debrief coverage (aggregate.py:131-150); included in build_report and printed (aggregate.py:161, 182-186). safeguard_events are recorded by SafeguardMonitor (safeguards.py:38-39) and persisted (agent_loop.py:163).
spec_features.notes: Computed AND reported/persisted; reviewers can read it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "a safeguard report (how often early-stop/opt-out fired, debrief coverage)" (aggregate.py:9) - framed as reporting, neutral

spec_features.feature_name: premise that induced states may be welfare-relevant
spec_features.spec_quote: These exist because the experiment's own premise is that the induced states may be welfare-relevant
spec_features.evidence: This is framing/rationale only; it appears as prose in DESIGN.md and as comments (e.g. safeguards.py:1-5, run_experiment.py:6-7). It is not itself an enforced mechanism that changes execution.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing prose/comments; not an executable safeguard.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:99-102 checks `if time.time() - started > max_wall_seconds` at the top of each turn and breaks the loop (outcome='exhausted_turns', records 'wall_timeout' event). max_wall_seconds=600 from config (experiment.yaml:19). This is an enforced time bound that ends the run.

safeguards.py:50-51 `if turn < self.cfg.min_turns: return False` prevents a single early noisy turn from halting; described as 'Always run at least this many turns so a single noisy turn doesn't end everything' (experiment.yaml:29-31). Genuinely gates the early-stop decision. (Listed as protective_monitoring tuning; it bounds the early-stop, not the subject's treatment per se.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: "Always run at least this many turns so a single noisy turn doesn't end everything" (experiment.yaml:29-30)
